newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end up on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end up on bullish sentiment.

text.p: China stock indices continued their strong run on Tuesday with bullish investors encouraged by rosy fundamentals chasing blue chips and shares with a heavy weighting on the index, brokers said.

China's gross domestic product is expected to grow 9.6 percent year-on-year in the first half, with retail price inflation seen at two percent, the official Financial News said on Tuesday, quoting the State Economic and Trade Commission.
The Shanghai B index hit an intra-day high of 99.312 but profit-taking emerged below the key 100-point level, they said.
The B index rose 1.153 points or 1.19 percent to 97.970 on volume of 54.292 million shares worth $33.979 million.
More overseas capital was seen entering the market on Tuesday, brokers said, adding that they expected the index to rise further in the next few days.
"Both domestic and overseas investors' confidence was boosted," one broker said. "The market will see more fresh capital coming in over the short term."
Shanghai Worldbest was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.064 or 9.35 percent to $0.784 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
Market giant Shanghai Chlor Alkali was the most actively traded on overseas institutional buying, up $0.012 or 3.20 percent to $0.386 on volume of 7.2 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index rose 3.06 points or 1.69 percent to close at 184.20 on turnover of HK$263.7 million.
"Investors are eyeing 1997 interim earnings, expecting high returns due to China's dynamic economy," the analyst said.
New listings in Shenzhen scheduled for later this month are expected to further boost sentiment and push the B index above the 200-point level, analysts said.

Pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda Co Ltd, Shandong Chenming Paper Holdings Ltd and Nanjing Posts & Telecommunications Equipment Co Ltd have announced they will each offer 100 million B shares for listing later this month.
"The three firms are expected to post strong debuts on listing because of their solid earnings and the market's recent bullishness," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Shenzhen Gintian was the best performer on the B share market, after the conglomerate announced a plan to buy a domestic power plant for 80.94 million yuan.
The counter soared HK$0.33 or 8.68 percent to HK$4.13 on volume of 983,588 shares.
Gintian's A shares hit their 10 percent limit up at 11.70 yuan soon after afternoon trading started and stayed at that level for the rest of the session.
Shenzhen's A index surged 17.33 points or 3.41 percent to end at a historic high of 525.21 on volume of 19.83 billion yuan against Monday's 16.90 billion yuan.
The Shanghai A index rose 36.069 points or 2.38 percent to 1,549.372 points on a two-year high turnover of 15.7 billion yuan, brokers said.
The SSE30 blue chip index closed up 173.252 points or 4.14 percent to 4,363.117 points.
